name: Trade war & tariffs
summary: China extended its truce measures to 10 Jan 2027 on 9 Nov, suspending its 24% tariff and new rare-earth controls
state: On 9 Nov China's commerce ministry extended its suspension of new rare-earth export controls to 10 Jan 2027, and its finance ministry kept a 24% tariff on US goods suspended for two months while a 10% levy stays (US News; The Star). The US has extended its own pauses to the same date. The truce is now short-term, with a Trump–Xi meeting expected at APEC in Shenzhen in mid-November, so Watch holds with an easing trend.
for_you: Tariff terms between the US and China are now set only to 10 Jan 2027. Exporters, importers and firms with Chinese supply chains remain exposed to any lapse.
rubric_hit: Major US–China tariff threats paused only to 10 Jan 2027; no new broad tariffs in force

sources.title: US News — China extends suspension of new rare earth controls until January
The Star — China extends suspension of rare earth export controls until January

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
